title: NASA Uranus satellite sheet: Ariel (UI) mass 12.9×10^20 kg, radius 581.1 x 577.9 x 577.7 km
summary: The Uranus satellite fact sheet lists Ariel (UI) at mass 12.9 × 10^20 kg and radius 581.1 x 577.9 x 577.7 km.
body: NASA's Uranus satellite fact sheet lists Ariel (UI) with mass 12.9 × 10^20 kg, radius 581.1 x 577.9 x 577.7 km, mean density 1,590 kg/m^3, and visual geometric albedo 0.39. Orbital parameters on the same sheet: Semi-major axis (10 3 km) = 190.90; Semi-major axis (Uranian Radii) = 7.469; Orbital Period * (days) = 2.520379; Rotation Period (days) = S; Inclination (degrees) = 0.04; Eccentricity = 0.0012. These are the cells printed on the sheet. The sheet does not say, on this row, which cells are a spacecraft measurement and which are an estimate. The sheet says R indicates retrograde motion, and S indicates synchronous rotation, the rotation period equal to the orbital period. Author of the sheet: Dr. David R. Williams, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center. Last Updated line: 11 March 2023.
